subject: cormorant
title: Japan Has Fished With Trained Birds for 1,300 Years. Here's the Trick

scenes.text: Fishermen in Japan have been fishing with birds for about 1,300 years.
At night on the Nagara River, a basket of burning wood hangs off the boat. The light draws river fish to the surface.
Then the cormorants dive. Each bird wears a cord, and a loose ring around its neck.
The ring is the trick. Small fish slip down, but a big fish gets stuck in the bird's throat.
The fisherman pulls the bird back in and it spits out the catch. One person can handle around ten birds at once.
Some of these fishermen work for the Imperial Household of Japan. The bird does the diving, and the human does the thinking.

description:
Fishermen in Japan have been fishing with birds for about 1,300 years.
On the Nagara River in Gifu, cormorant fishing happens at night under a burning basket of wood that draws fish to the surface. Each bird wears a cord and a ring around the neck, so small fish go down but big fish stay in the throat, and the fisher pulls the bird back in to take the catch. Some of the fishers are officials of the Imperial Household Agency.
Would you trust a bird with your dinner?
first_comment: Cormorant fishing on the Nagara River is called ukai. Would you trust a bird with your dinner?
